_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with advanced unresectable or metastatic NSCLC, and adults with advanced unresectable or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, harboring an NRG1 gene fusion with disease progression on or after prior systemic therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, multinational study, with a dose-escalation phase followed by a single-arm, multiple-indication expansion phase.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with advanced or metastatic NRG1 fusion-positive NSCLC or pancreatic adenocarcinoma who had disease progression on or after prior systemic therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed overall response rate (ORR) per RECIST 1.1 by blinded independent central review (BICR), supported by duration of response (DOR).
pivotal_trials.n: Efficacy: 64 previously treated NSCLC patients and 30 PDAC patients

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were diarrhea, musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, nausea, infusion-related reactions, dyspnea, rash, constipation, vomiting, abdominal pain, and edema. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 25% of patients who received BIZENGRI.
target_moa: Bispecific antibody that binds the extracellular domains of HER2 and HER3, blocking HER2:HER3 dimerization and preventing NRG1 binding to HER3, thereby inhibiting downstream PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling.
modality: bispecific (HER2- and HER3-directed IgG1 bispecific antibody)

boxed_warning.content: Embryo-Fetal Toxicity: exposure during pregnancy can cause embryo-fetal harm; advise patients of the risk and the need for effective contraception.

rems.type: No REMS required; no significant safety concerns warranting a REMS were identified during the BLA review.

companion_dx_detail: Patient selection is based on presence of an NRG1 gene fusion, but no FDA-approved companion diagnostic test is currently available.

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee.

description.text: Added indication for advanced unresectable or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring an NRG1 gene fusion with progression after prior systemic therapy

citations.quote: BIZENGRI is indicated for the treatment of adults with advanced unresectable or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring a neuregulin 1 (NRG1) gene fusion with disease progression on or after prior systemic therapy.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR), considered reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: the recommendation for accelerated approval is primarily supported by overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) results of Study MCLA-128-CL01 (eNRGy), which are considered reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Continue the eNRGy study to verify and describe clinical benefit — a trial in at least 100 evaluable NSCLC patients and at least 50 evaluable PDAC patients with NRG1 fusions.

summary.text: BLA 761352 received Priority review and was granted accelerated approval based on ORR and DOR from the single-arm eNRGy study; the program had Breakthrough Therapy Designation (NRG1+ PDAC and NRG1+ NSCLC), Fast Track, and Orphan Drug designation, with continued approval contingent on confirmatory verification of clinical benefit.

To characterize response rate and duration, patients will be followed for at least 12 months from the onset of response.

requirement.text: 4727-3 Conduct a comprehensive integrated safety analysis in a sufficient number of adult patients from clinical trials to adequately characterize the known serious risks of infusion-related reactions/hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, and left ventricular dysfunction following exposure to zenocutuzumab. The integrated safety analysis should include all adverse events, major safety events, dose-reductions, dose interruptions, and withdrawals, when all patients have completed at least two years of treatment with zenocutuzumab or withdrew earlier.

requirement.text: 4727-4 Develop and validate a neutralizing antibody (NAb) assay and submit a full validation report of the developed NAb assay. The assay format should be adequately justified to be suitable for the detection of NAbs. This NAb assay will be used to test available confirmed anti-drug antibody positive samples from banked and ongoing clinical studies. Include the updated NAb results analyzed using the validated NAb assay to address the effects of neutralizing antibody on the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, safety, and effectiveness of zenocutuzumab.
